items.name: Rectangle primitive (stroke + fill + opacity)
items.spec:
Add `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.{h,cpp}` — screen-agnostic Clay helper for a flat-colored rectangle with optional stroke and optional fill opacity. API shape (final names yours; spirit of the constraints binding):

- Take ALL color/width values as REQUIRED parameters (compile-time, not opts-struct defaults) — match the precedent set by commit 63c779d. No lobby-coupled defaults.
- Knobs: fillPaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no fill' sentinel), fillOpacity (0.0–1.0 or palette-alpha-index), strokePaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no stroke'), strokeWidth (Uint8, fixed 1 px is fine for now if you want to simplify), plus sizing (caller-provided width/height OR sized-by-parent if used inside a flex container).
- The primitive emits ONE Clay element with `.backgroundColor` and `.border` configured from the params. No CUSTOM render command unless opacity-blending requires it (see C1).
- Add a render test at `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/rectangle_test.cpp` that renders 4 variants: stroke-only, fill-only, fill+stroke, fill-with-opacity-over-an-existing-color. Wired through the JSON-lines control op pattern used by other primitive tests.
- Test references at `tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test/` (reference.png + run.sh).
items.pass_check: cmake --build build -j green. tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test/run.sh PASS. Header + impl have no #include of world.h/lobby.h/config.h/MapDownloader. Compiler refuses callers that forget to pass color or stroke params.

items.name: Bridge: alpha-blended rectangle fills via palette alphaed LUT
items.spec:
The current Clay bridge dispatches RECTANGLE by writing a single palette index per pixel — no alpha. For C0's `fillOpacity`, the bridge must route to the renderer's existing palette-blend path. Read `clients/silencer/src/render/palette.cpp` (look for `alphaed`) to understand the LUT: `alphaed[palette][src*256 + dst]` returns the blended palette index. Each rectangle pixel at opacity α maps to `alphaed[…][srcColor*256 + dstColor]` with α as the LUT bank selector (or, simpler first cut: pick one alpha level for now, e.g. 50%, and document that opacity is currently quantized to that single level — full N-level alpha can come later if needed).

Extend the bridge in `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/clay_bridge.cpp`. If the simplest path is a new CustomKind (e.g. `CustomKind::FillBlend`) that the Rectangle primitive routes through when `fillOpacity < 1.0`, that's fine — but prefer just enhancing the existing RECTANGLE dispatch to read the userData for an optional opacity hint.

Add a smoke test: a fully-opaque red rect underneath a 50%-opaque blue rect should produce a known mid-tone palette index in the overlap region. Pixdiff against a hand-crafted reference < 0.5%.
items.pass_check: Build green. Existing `rectangle_test` from C0 still passes. New `tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_alpha_test/run.sh` PASS with pixdiff < 0.5% vs reference.png.

items.name: Document lobby BG rectangle coordinates
items.spec:
Visually inspect `/tmp/lobby_bg.png` (regenerate via the Python decoder if missing — see RALPH.md appendix). Identify every distinct bright-green stroked rectangle in the chrome (NOT the decorative texture inside them, NOT the film-strip sphere lights). Expected: roughly 4–6 rectangles — outer frame, title bar strip, character panel area, chat panel area (NOTE: chat may be an upside-down-L overlapping character — call that out), right pane area. Maybe a top-right decorative rect.

For each rectangle, record: (id-name, x, y, width, height, stroke palette index sampled from the sprite at a stroke pixel). Commit as `docs/plans/lobby-chrome-rectangles.md`. Include a short note on the upside-down-L topology with your recommendation (compose two rects vs. polygon primitive vs. rework). This document is the reference for C3–C6.

items.name: Outer frame + title bar rectangles (chrome relocated via flex)
items.spec:
Using the Rectangle primitive (C0) and the coordinates from C2, emit two Clay-drawn rectangles: an outer frame around the working area and a title bar strip across the top. The existing TitleBar chrome elements (title text 'Silencer', version 'v.X', map-name overlay, Go Back BankButton) currently live as four separate `floating @ROOT (x, y)` elements in `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby_clay/lobby_clay_screen.cpp` (search `LobbyTitle`, `LobbyVer`, `LobbyMapName`, `LobbyGoBackWrap`). Relocate them INSIDE the new title bar rectangle using flex layout — `LEFT_TO_RIGHT`, gaps, alignment. Don't keep `floating @ROOT` for title-bar elements after this iteration.

The LobbyBg sprite STAYS emitted underneath in this iteration (so misalignment between your new rectangles and the baked ones is visible). Don't drop it yet — that's C7.

Picking exact pixel coords: aim to match the baked rectangle positions to within ~2 px on each edge so the chrome looks coherent during the transition. The Rectangle stroke color comes from C2's documented sample.

items.name: Right pane rectangle (variant subtree inside)
items.spec:
Emit a Rectangle for the right pane area. The right pane is variant-based: one of `BuildGameSelectPanelTree`, `BuildGameCreatePanelTree`, `BuildGameJoinPanelTree`, `BuildGameTechPanelTree` emits inside it at any given time (mutually exclusive). Each panel currently uses `floating @ROOT (x, y)` for its child elements (search `GSel`, `GCrt`, `GJoin`, `GTech`).

Relocate ALL FOUR variant subtrees inside the new Rectangle via flex layout. Each is its own refactor. Keep existing primitive composition. The previous IMAGE-based right-pane border (bank 7 idx 8 — emitted as `GSelRightBorder` and equivalents) becomes redundant — remove.

LobbyBg still STAYS underneath this iteration. This is the largest iteration of the milestone — budget accordingly. If any one of the four variants is blocked, leave passes=false with a documented obstacle and the other variants partially done in a commit.

items.spec:

If you need a background color behind the panels to avoid a stark black (e.g., to mirror the legacy dark-grey-ish behind-chrome), set a `.backgroundColor` on the LobbyRoot — but do NOT introduce a new sprite. Flat color only.
